prompt_text: Where should I buy tires in Pleasanton CA and who does the best installation?
answer_verbatim:
I can help — do you want specific shop names/addresses nearby now, or general guidance on where to buy and how to choose an installer? Quick summary, then a short checklist you can use when calling or booking.

Short recommendations (Pleasanton area)
- Costco Tire Center — often cheapest for common tire sizes if you’re a Costco member; reliable mounting/balancing and generally good warranty handling, but can be busy and appointment windows fill fast.
- Discount Tire (nearby in Dublin/Fremont areas) — very good customer service, price-matching on many brands, and fast installs; technicians are experienced and they’re good about fit/TPMS/torque.
- Major chains: Firestone Complete Auto Care, Pep Boys — convenient, nationwide warranties and alignment services; quality varies by location, so check local reviews.
- Independent/local tire shops — can be the best installers (more attention to detail, experienced techs) if you pick a well-reviewed shop. Look for ASE certified techs and shops with many recent 4–5 star reviews on Google/Yelp.

What to ask/confirm before buying/installing
- Is the quoted price for the tire just the tire or “mounted & balanced” included?
- Is alignment included or available at a discounted rate (you should get an alignment after new tires)?
- Road hazard warranty / free flat repairs / lifetime rotations — what’s included and for how long?
- Do they reset/inspect TPMS and torque lug nuts to spec after installation?
- Are the installers ASE-certified and do they use a computerized alignment rack?
- Appointment lead time and how long installation will take.

How to choose between shops
- Price + included services (mount/balance, valve stems, lug nut torque, TPMS, alignment)
- Recent local reviews (Google and Yelp)
- Warranty handling reputation (important if you need a replacement)
- Convenience of location/appointment times

If you want, I can:
- Look up highly rated tire shops in Pleasanton and give addresses, phone numbers and current Google/Yelp ratings; or
- Compare quotes from 2–3 shops (if you give your tire size or car make/model and any brand preferences and whether you have a Costco membership).

Which would you prefer?
